title: Capacity Whisperboard — Shadow Region Runbook & Weekly Checkin
content:
Purpose
Quick weekly checkin for the ‘whisperboard’ workflow: lightweight, low-risk capacity experiments that run in a shadow region (non-production routing) to validate prewarmed pools, packing heuristics, and fallback behaviors before we push to canary in prod. This doc captures notes from 2026-08-11 run, open action items, and small runbook tweaks.

High level summary (one line)
Shadow-region prewarm + densification test showed 18% median cold-start latency improvement for batched text-gen paths but introduced 6% increase in backfill queue times for low-priority pods. Acceptable trade if we adjust backfill policy.

What we ran this week
- Scenario: 90m window (04:00–05:30 UTC) synthetic burst to the shadow region (west-us-2-shadow) using the q8_1 model family and 512 max-length workloads.
- Controls: normal routing disabled; traffic duplicated from prod via mirroring lambda; no real customer requests served.
- Variants: 3 packing configs — baseline (current), densify-light (pack 1.4x GPUs), densify-aggressive (pack 1.8x, opportunistic migration).
- Observability probes: token-level latency, KV-cache hit-rate, prefill warmup time, pod preemption counts, backfill queue depth, GPU memory fragmentation metric.

Key observations
- Prewarming: both densify variants reduced first-token latency by ~18% median (baseline 85ms -> 70ms). 95th p95 improved similarly but p99 unchanged.
- KV-cache: hit rate rose slightly (3–5pp) under densify variants due to better locality in request routing, but the effect is model/seed dependent.
- Backfill/backpressure: densify-aggressive produced more frequent ephemeral preemptions of low-priority pods; backfill queue depth spiked by ~6% and queueing time increased for the background job class.
- GPU memory fragmentation: densify-aggressive exhibited more fragmentation, leading to small (~2%) increase in failure-to-allocate errors during peak ramp (we hit retry loops in the runtime).
- Cost proxy: per-token GPU-time decreased for dense runs; however, wasted cycles due to migration retries offset some savings. Net estimate: 7–9% cost reduction under steady bursts, uncertain under noisy mixes.

Incidents / anomalies
- 04:22 UTC: transient spike in allocation failures (runtime logging showing KV cache inconsistency on node drain). Mitigated by increasing drain-timeout from 12s to 28s for the shadow pool; we need to quantify impact on user-facing drains before applying in prod. Ticketed: JIRA-OPS-1428.
- 05:05 UTC: a mirroring lambda mis-routed ~0.5% of requests to the production autoscaling group due to stale routing config; no customer impact observed but we filed a hotfix to pin mirror targets.

Decisions proposed (quick)
- Accept densify-light as default in shadow prewarming flows for further 2-week A/B tests. Rationale: sweet spot for latency vs backfill. Vote: Omar +1, Lucía +1, Maya +1, Arjun 0 (needs more data).
- Do not promote densify-aggressive without mitigations for fragmentation and backfill throttles.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Arjun: run mixed-traffic simulation (30% small 32-token, 70% 512-token) on densify-light and report cost delta by 2026-08-19.
- Lucía: add a runtime guard to detect excessive fragmentation and automatically reduce packing intensity (proposal draft) — due 2026-08-18.
- Kai: update drain-timeout doc and run limited prod-sim with extended drain window (safety checklist) — due 2026-08-17.
- Maya: coordinate a short tabletop (15m) with SRE and Serving Runtime to review mirroring lambda hardening — scheduled 2026-08-13 10:00 UTC.

Lightweight runbook tweaks (for whisperboard shadow runs)
- Mirror gateway should now include an explicit "mirror-target-pin" property to avoid accidental fallthroughs. Add to runbook step 2.
- Shadow pool drain-timeout default: 28s (was 12s). Note: do not change prod pools until after the mixed-traffic sim.
- Observability: add a per-run fragmentation gauge and alert if > 4% allocation-failure-rate for > 2m.

Questions / Unknowns (notes-to-self style)
- How will densify-light behave with many small chat-style requests in burst? Hypothesis: may reduce throughput for small requests due to batching alignment. Need microbench.
- Does increased KV locality hold for multilingual workloads where token distribution is more diffuse?
- Are there corner cases where migration retries cascade and cause a domino of preempts? Need to stress with longer windows (4h).

Followups for product & solutions teams
- Solutions: prepare an FAQ paragraph on what shadow-region means for customers and how prewarming/densification relates to SLA (for sales/CS calls). Tiny draft attached to linked_artifacts.
- Product: consider a pack-intensity knob exposed in Redwood Console per-pool (low/auto/high) with warnings about backfill implications.

Misc notes / context log (raw)
- Slack snippets: "mirrors should never talk to prod ASGs" — added to runbook.
- Git PR: priming-experiments/pull/87 includes densify tuning values and unit tests for allocator heuristics.
- Cost model used: internal cost-proxy v3 (see confluence link).

Meeting attendees (today)
Maya Chen (owner), Omar Patel, Lucía Gomez, Arjun Srinivasan, Kai Tan, SRE on-call (Samir Rao joined for incident debrief).

Next steps
- Small A/B for densify-light for two weeks against standard prewarm (mirrored only), then evaluate: latency distribution, backfill impact, per-token cost, and fragmentation incidents.
- If green, schedule a low-risk canary rollout to a single low-traffic region and observe for 48h with SRE shadowing.

Quick log (timestamps)
- 03:55: started mirror, validated metric probes
- 04:21: allocation failures spike -> increased drain timeout
- 04:50: densify-light shows stable p50/p95 gains
- 05:05: mirror mis-route -> revert lambda pinning, no prod impact
- 05:30: stopped run, collected traces and heap dumps

If you have corrections / more logs to attach, paste below or add GH link.

-- Maya
